scope: Destination loading, optional automatic page reading, transparent field editing, choice navigation and page boundaries.

topics.title: Automatic reading and transparent fields
details: Options, Web browsing now includes Automatic page reading, on by default. The loaded message and virtual viewer remain available when it is off. Say Automatic page reading on or off, Enable automatic page reading, or Disable automatic page reading. Read page explicitly reads the page regardless of this setting.

Tab, arrows and quick keys automatically make text fields ready for typing and combo/list boxes ready for selection. No additional Enter or forms-mode command is required. Tab/Shift+Tab saves a text field and moves on; arrows leave single-line fields, and leave multiline fields at their text boundaries. Outside fields, ordinary page reading resumes.

Combo/list boxes accept arrows, Home/End and first-letter cycling. Disabled options are skipped. Say next option, previous option, first option, last option, select option followed by its label, or choose option beginning with a letter. Native and labelled ARIA choice widgets are supported; popup lists do not add a second Tab stop.

topics.title: Page readiness and virtual-view refresh
details: Following a result waits for navigation, destination document readiness and readable content, including new tabs and delayed single-page transitions, before capturing the virtual view. Page loaded identifies a ready document; a partially loading document is reported separately. Automatic narration reads the first chunk and Continue reading reads more.

Later URL, document and DOM changes update the virtual buffer without requiring a spoken Read page request. Incidental text updates preserve the reading position and continuation. Page updates can be detected while old page narration is playing; active field edits, lists and pending reviews are protected from background refresh.

topics.title: Link roles, Escape and page boundaries
details: Web links announce Link before the label during quick navigation, arrow reading and link lists. List first-letter shortcuts continue to use the link label. The main-menu item is now Web browser.

Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End reach the exact beginning/end of the virtual page. Voice equivalents include Top of page, Beginning of page, Start of page, Bottom of page and End of page, with Go to, Move to or Jump to also accepted.

Escape from the page returns to the main menu. Escape first closes an element list or cancels staged field editing; a subsequent Escape leaves the browser activity. Voice Close list, Cancel field editing, Leave website, Close browser and Exit web browser provide matching actions.

topics.title: Preserved safeguards and release verification
details: Automatic field focus does not submit a form. Consequential buttons retain review safeguards, passwords stay masked and are never included in the virtual text, and leaving an unchanged rich field preserves its markup. Keyboard page-boundary navigation can save privately typed input; voice navigation cannot expose a staged password.

Help and all versioned What’s New formats document these changes. Regression tests cover the new behavior; live Windows fixtures exercise delayed pages, new tabs, native/ARIA choices, physical typing and page-boundary shortcuts across Firefox, Chrome, Edge and Brave. Site-specific beta testing remains necessary.
